reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows that Mn moments switch between positive and negative values and that pure Mn in fcc would be magnetically frustrated, supporting the premise that Mn induces magnetic frustration. However, E1 provides no evidence linking magnetic frustration to an increase in effective SFE, nor does it address how SFE changes upon Mn removal or how SFE affects twinning/transformation and mechanical properties. Thus, only the first premise is directly supported, while the remaining key premises lack specific prior evidence.
premises: Mn induces magnetic frustration in equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi
Magnetic frustration raises the effective stacking fault energy (SFE)
Higher SFE suppresses deformation-induced nanotwinning and fcc-to-hcp transformation
Removing or reducing Mn lowers SFE and relaxes magnetic frustration
Lower SFE enhances twin nucleation and transformation-induced plasticity, improving work hardening and ductility
